summary: Midday 5xx wave caused by NVMe I/O saturation on shared model artifact pool
description:
Issue summary:
Midday (approx 12:05-12:45 UTC) elevated 5xx rate observed for multiple OmniHealth dedicated tenants in us-west-2. API gateway returned a mix of 502 and 504 to client calls; downstream serving-runtime logs showed long syscall stalls while reading model artifacts from the shared NVMe pool, followed by watchdog-triggered runtime restarts.

Impact:
- OmniHealth reported ~40% of requests failed with 5xx during the window, impacting clinical ingestion pipelines.
- Customer observed request timeouts and partial completions for streaming sessions.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant (OmniHealth), prod-us-west (us-west-2)
- Serving runtime: realtime-runtime v1.9.2 (quantized kernels enabled)
- Storage: shared NVMe artifact pool mounted on dedicated nodes with NFS metadata layer

Steps to reproduce (investigation method):
1) Replay a subset of OmniHealth traffic in staging prewarming config against same model and artifact layout.
2) Trigger high-concurrency prefetch (concurrent artifact reads for large prompt sets) while running iostat and perf.
3) Observe long synchronous read latencies on /mnt/artifacts and increased iowait on host.

Relevant logs & signals:
- Grafana alert: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alerts/prod-iowait?panelId=7 (spike at 12:06 UTC)
- Sentry event: runtime/serve: watchdog.restart (count=18) https://sentry.redwood.ai/issue/987654
- Example runtime log excerpt: "blocking read: 2370ms on /mnt/artifacts/gptx-4-quant/kv.bin"
- Edge/API gateway logs: repeated 502 upstream_read_timeout with upstream_id runtime-az-west-3
- Host metrics: iowait jumped from 2% -> 58% on nvme-pool-03 at 12:05 UTC

Initial mitigation performed:
- Scoped and throttled tenant prefetch (rate limit of 5 concurrent artifact fetches) at 12:12 UTC — immediate reduction in new 5xx occurrences.
- Evacuated two noisy pods from nvme-pool-03 to warm nodes at 12:20 UTC to relieve host-level I/O pressure.

Notes on customer communication:
- Support notified OmniHealth CS at 12:25 UTC with current mitigations and ETA for full remediation.
- Customer on call; provided request logs and advised to temporarily reduce batch prefetch concurrency for scheduled jobs.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis A: Large parallel artifact prefetch from tenant jobs saturated NVMe pool IOPS leading to syscall blocking in serving runtime.
Evidence: iostat and host top show high nvme read latencies concurrent with 5xx spike.
Hypothesis B: NVMe firmware compaction cycle coincidentally triggered — low likelihood; firmware logs show no compaction events in window.

Collected artifacts: host iostat (nvme-pool-03), runtime core dumps (none), watchdog restart traces, NFS metadata latency metrics.
Analysis: blocking reads originated inside kernel copy path while reading multiple KV shard files concurrently. Prefetch code path issued blocking open/read for artifacts; refactor to async read reduces tail latency under contention.
Related history: similar symptoms previously in SUP-661234 (apigw-vpc-peering-signal-loss) but root cause there was different (network). Added label to avoid noisy correlations.
resolution_notes:
Root cause: tenant-driven concurrent synchronous artifact prefetch overloaded shared NVMe artifact pool causing high host iowait and blocking reads inside serving runtime.
Fixes applied:
1) Short-term: applied tenant prefetch concurrency throttle (API-layer) and evacuated noisy pods; reduced 5xx within 10 minutes.
2) Medium-term: rolled out non-blocking async artifact prefetch implementation (runtime PR github.com/redwood/realtime-runtime/pull/1823) across dedicated fleet (canary -> full rollout completed 2026-03-14).
3) Long-term: capacity and QoS: created NVMe pool IOPS reservations per-tenant and added an autoscaling policy for artifact-serving backends.
Follow-ups:
- Postmortem document scheduled: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/NVMe+hotspot+runbook (owner: Priya Nair)
- Add alert to detect sustained nvme_p99_read_ms > 300ms for >5m (owner: infra-alerting)
